# 404 Memory Found

> 404 Memory Found is a nostalgia blog about the technology, games, websites and companies of the 90s and 2000s: what they cost, why they won or lost, and what happened to them.

Every article is written under a pen name by the site's editorial team, sourced from primary documents (company filings, court records, contemporary reporting, museum collections) listed at the end of each post, and dated. Full text of every article, in Markdown: https://404memoryfound.com/llms-full.txt

## Hub pages
- [All posts](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/): every article, newest first
- [About and editorial policy](https://404memoryfound.com/about.html)
- [RSS feed](https://404memoryfound.com/feed.xml)

## Business Blunders
- [Is SkyMall Still Around in 2026? Yes, Online Only](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/skymall-still-around-who-owns-it.html): SkyMall is still around in 2026 as an online store. C&A Marketing bought the bankrupt in-flight catalog at auction in 2015 for $1.9 million.
- [Why Montgomery Ward Failed and Who Owns It Now](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/montgomery-ward-failed-who-owns-it.html): Montgomery Ward closed all 250 stores in 2001 after 128 years. Colony Brands has owned the name since 2008 and sells it online at wards.com.
- [Who Owns Packard Bell Now? Acer Revived the Brand](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/packard-bell-computer-brand-today.html): Packard Bell is owned by Acer, which relaunched the dead 1990s PC brand in September 2026 with a 499 euro laptop sold everywhere but the US.
- [Is Tower Records Still Around? Online and in Japan](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/tower-records-still-around.html): Tower Records is still around as an online store and a chain in Japan, but all 89 US stores closed after the 2006 bankruptcy auction.
- [Who Owns eToys.com Now? Toys R Us Bought the Name](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/etoys-com-who-owns-it-now.html): Toys R Us has owned eToys.com since February 2009, paying a reported $2.15 million. The original eToys died in 2001, two years after a $76 IPO pop.
- [Broadcast.com: The $5.7 Billion Site Yahoo Shut Down](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/broadcast-com-yahoo-billion-dollar-deal.html): Yahoo bought Broadcast.com for $5.7 billion in 1999 and closed the service by 2002. The company had booked $22.4 million of revenue in 1998.
- [Is Angelfire Still Online? Lycos Closed It in 2026](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-angelfire-still-online.html): Angelfire is not still online. Lycos took the free web host down on April 24, 2026, after a January outage and 30 days of notice.
- [Why Discovery Zone Failed and What's Left in 2026](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/discovery-zone-failed-indoor-playground.html): Discovery Zone failed after two bankruptcies and closed for good by the end of 2001. One unaffiliated center still uses the name in 2026.
- [How Many Rainforest Cafes Are Left? 16 in the US](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/rainforest-cafe-locations-left.html): Rainforest Cafe is down to 16 US restaurants in 11 states in 2026, from a peak of 59. Landry's owns it, and the Paris location closes in November.
- [Who Owns Kinko's Now? FedEx Retired the Brand](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-kinkos-still-around.html): Kinko's is gone in the US: FedEx bought it for $2.4 billion, then took an $891 million charge in 2008 to stop using the name.
- [Why G4 TV Failed Twice: The 1,000-Viewer Collapse](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/g4-tv-failed-twice.html): G4 TV failed twice. Comcast unplugged the gaming channel on December 31, 2014, revived it in November 2021, and shut it down again in October 2022.
- [Is Photobucket Still Around? Why Your Photos Vanished](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-photobucket-still-around.html): Photobucket is still around in 2026, but only as paid storage: free accounts ended in June 2023 and plans now start at $5 a month for 1TB.
- [Who Owns Game Informer Now? Gunzilla Games Does](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/who-owns-game-informer-now.html): Game Informer is owned by Gunzilla Games, which bought it in March 2025 after GameStop killed it in 2024. Issue 381 marks 35 years in print.
- [How Many KB Toys Stores Are Left? Zero Since 2009](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/kb-toys-stores-left.html): How many KB Toys stores are left? Zero. All 461 closed by February 9, 2009, and the brand now survives online and at a Comic-Con booth.
- [Where Is FAO Schwarz Now? Inside Rockefeller Center](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/fao-schwarz-store-rockefeller-center.html): FAO Schwarz is still open, but not on Fifth Avenue. The flagship moved to 30 Rockefeller Plaza in 2018, and Nordstrom shops followed in 2026.
- [Is Woolworth Still in Business? Only as Foot Locker](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-woolworth-still-in-business.html): Woolworth is still in business, but only as Foot Locker: it renamed itself in 2001, four years after shutting all 400 US five-and-dime stores.
- [Who Owns Sharper Image Now? No Stores Since 2008](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/who-owns-sharper-image-now.html): Sharper Image is owned by ThreeSixty Group, which paid $100 million for the name in December 2016. No stores have existed since the 2008 collapse.
- [Is the Disney Store Still Open? 21 Left in 2026](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-disney-store-still-open.html): The Disney Store is still open, but only about 21 locations are left in North America in 2026, down from 747 stores at the 1999 peak.
- [How Many Sam Goody Stores Are Left? Exactly One](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/sam-goody-stores-left.html): Exactly one Sam Goody store is left in 2026, at a mall in Medford, Oregon. Musicland closed 226 of them in a single month in 2006.
- [Does Nokia Still Make Phones? Who Makes Them Now](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/does-nokia-still-make-phones.html): Does Nokia still make phones? No. Nokia sold its handset business to Microsoft in 2013, and the last Nokia smartphones were pulled in January 2025.
- [Who Owns Borders Now? The $13.9 Million Brand Sale](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/who-owns-borders-now-bookstore.html): Borders closed its last US stores in September 2011. Barnes & Noble owns the name now, bought for $13.9 million with 48 million customer records.
- [Is Hollywood Video Still Around? Every Store Closed](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-hollywood-video-still-around.html): Hollywood Video is gone. Movie Gallery liquidated the last 1,900-plus US stores in 2010, and its late fees chased 3.3 million customers for years.
- [Is Barnes and Noble Still Open? 720+ Stores in 2026](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-barnes-and-noble-still-open.html): Barnes and Noble is still open and growing: more than 720 US stores in 2026, with 60 more planned. Elliott has owned the chain since 2019.
- [Who Owns Claire's Now? The $140 Million Buyout](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/who-owns-claires-now.html): Claire's is owned by Ames Watson, which bought the chain out of bankruptcy in 2025 for about $140 million. Roughly 900 stores are still open.
- [How Many Boston Market Locations Are Left in 2026?](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/boston-market-locations-left.html): Boston Market is down to about six listed locations in 2026, and only three answered the phone. It had 1,143 restaurants in 1998. Here is what closed them.
- [Is GameStop Still in Business? 1,598 Stores Left](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-gamestop-still-in-business.html): GameStop is still in business in 2026, but it closed 727 US stores in one year and ended January with 1,598 left. Games are now under 12% of sales.
- [Is Redbox Still Around? Why Kiosks Are Still There](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-redbox-still-around-kiosks.html): Redbox is gone: its parent was liquidated in July 2024 and all 24,000 kiosks went dark. Thousands still stand because removal runs about $500 each.
- [Who Owns Yahoo Now? The $5 Billion Apollo Takeover](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/who-owns-yahoo-now.html): Yahoo is owned by Apollo Global Management, which paid about $5 billion in 2021. Verizon kept 10 percent. Microsoft once offered $44.6 billion.
- [Does Yahoo Answers Still Exist? Why It Shut Down](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/does-yahoo-answers-still-exist.html): Yahoo Answers does not still exist. It went read-only on April 20, 2021 and closed on May 4, 2021, 15 years after launch. Here is what survived.
- [Who Owns Napster in 2026? Every Owner Since 2001](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/who-owns-napster-now.html): Napster is owned by Napster Corporation, formerly Infinite Reality, which paid $207 million in 2025 and killed the music service on January 1, 2026.
- [Is Sega Still Making Games? Life After the Dreamcast](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-sega-still-making-games.html): Is Sega still making games? Yes. Its games arm sold 326.6 billion yen worth last fiscal year, and Sonic 3 grossed 492.2 million dollars.
- [Is Kmart Still Open? The 3 Stores Left in 2026](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-kmart-still-open-stores-left.html): Is Kmart still open in 2026? Yes, but only three stores are left: Miami, Guam and St. Thomas. It had 2,114 the day it filed for bankruptcy.
- [Is CompUSA Still Around? What Happened to the Chain](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-compusa-still-around.html): Is CompUSA still around? No. The chain sold its last 103 stores in December 2007, and the brand was written off for $35.3 million in 2012.
- [Who Owns Sears Now, and How Many Stores Are Left?](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/who-owns-sears-now-stores-left.html): Sears is owned by Eddie Lampert's Transformco and it is still trading. The last count found five full-line stores left, down from about 3,500.
- [Who Owns Atari Now? The Brand That Refuses to Die](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/who-owns-atari-now.html): Atari is owned by Atari SA in Paris and run by Wade Rosen. The brand sold for $5 million in 1998 and booked about $65 million last year.
- [Is Toys R Us Still in Business? What Survived 2018](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-toys-r-us-still-in-business.html): Toys R Us closed all 735 US stores on June 29, 2018. The brand survived: WHP Global owns it, and 1,664 stores now trade in 35 countries.
- [Is Palm Still a Company? From Pilot to a $349 Phone](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-palm-still-a-company.html): Is Palm still a company? No. HP bought it for $1.2 billion in 2010, sold webOS to LG, and TCL has owned the dormant Palm brand since 2014.
- [Is Blockbuster Still Open? The Last Store in 2026](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-blockbuster-still-open-last-store.html): Is Blockbuster still open? Yes, but only one store, in Bend, Oregon. Who owns the brand in 2026, how 9,000 stores became one, and what it sells.
- [Does AOL Still Exist? What You Get for $10 a Month](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/does-aol-still-exist-today.html): Does AOL still exist? Yes. Italy's Bending Spoons bought it for about $1.5 billion in January 2026, and dial-up died on September 30, 2025.
- [How Compaq Lost the PC Business It Helped Invent](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/compaq-lost-pc-business-hp-merger.html): Compaq went from a pie-shop sketch in 1982 to the world's biggest PC maker, then sold itself to HP for $25 billion. Here is what broke first.
- [Why Iridium Failed: The $5 Billion Satellite Phone](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/iridium-satellite-phone-failure.html): Iridium put 66 satellites in orbit for about $5 billion, opened for business in 1998, and filed for bankruptcy nine months later. It sold for $25 million.
- [The Beanie Babies Bubble: How a $5 Toy Went Bust](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/beanie-babies-bubble-what-happened.html): Beanie Babies were a $5 toy people traded like stocks in 1998. How Ty Inc. built the bubble, why it burst in 1999, and what the bears are worth now.
- [Why the Sega 32X Failed: The $159.99 Add-On Flop](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-sega-32x-add-on.html): The Sega 32X launched November 21, 1994 at $159.99, sold about 665,000 units, shipped 40 games, and was cleared out at $19.95 before dying in 1996.
- [theGlobe.com Today: The 606% IPO That Left a Shell](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-theglobe-com-dot-com-ipo.html): theGlobe.com is now an empty shell company with no employees and $15,115 in cash. Its 1998 IPO closed up 606 percent, a record that still stands.
- [What Happened to Excite, the Search Engine That Turned Down Google for $750,000](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-excite-search-engine-google.html): In 1999, Excite was worth $35 billion and had the chance to buy Google for $750,000. CEO George Bell said no. The full story is more complicated, and a lot more interesting, than the punchline suggests.
- [Why the TurboGrafx-16 Won Japan and Lost America](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-turbografx-16-nec-forgotten-console.html): NEC's TurboGrafx-16 ruled Japan as the PC Engine but sold just 750,000 US units by 1991. Konami owns the library now, and a Mini shipped in 2020.
- [What Happened to PointCast and the 1990s Push Technology Boom](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-pointcast-push-technology.html): In 1997, News Corporation offered $450 million for a company that delivered headlines through a screensaver. Two years later it sold for $7 million. The full story of push technology's rise and collapse.
- [How the Nintendo NES Saved Video Games After the 1983 Crash](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/how-nintendo-nes-saved-video-games-1983-crash.html): In 1985, American retailers had given up on video games. Then a Japanese toy company shipped a gray plastic box with a robot, called it an entertainment system, and resurrected an entire industry. This is the full story of how the NES pulled gaming back from the dead.
- [What Happened to Standalone GPS Devices: TomTom and the Smartphone Killer](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-standalone-gps-tomtom-garmin-magellan.html): In 2008, the world bought 42 million standalone GPS devices. By 2014, the category was effectively dead. The story of how a free Android feature, a Cold War satellite system, and an $11 billion map data war ended an entire consumer electronics market.
- [What Happened to Wine.com and the Internet Wine Wars](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-wine-com-internet-wine-wars.html): Three companies burned through more than $200M trying to sell wine online between 1995 and 2001. The smallest one ended up owning the Wine.com domain.
- [What Happened to Prodigy, the Online Service That Beat AOL to America](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-prodigy-online-service.html): Before AOL, before the web, two of the biggest companies in America spent over a billion dollars trying to teach the country how to go online. Prodigy got there first, then lost everything.
- [What Happened to the 3DO, the $700 Console That Bombed](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-3do-700-dollar-console.html): In 1993, a console hit shelves at $699.99 and promised to be the VHS of gaming. Instead, the 3DO became one of the most spectacular flops in video game history. Here is the full story.
- [What Happened to Microsoft Bob, the Friendly Interface That Failed](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-microsoft-bob-friendly-interface.html): In 1995, Microsoft tried to replace the desktop with a cartoon house full of talking pets. It sold around 58,000 copies and got pulled from shelves within a year. Here is what really happened.
- [What Happened to Kodak, the Company That Invented the Digital Camera Then Chose to Ignore It](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-kodak-digital-camera-bankruptcy.html): Kodak controlled 90% of the American film market, employed over 145,000 people, and invented the digital camera in 1975. Then it spent three decades pretending digital photography wasn't coming.
- [What Happened to the Segway, the Invention That Was Supposed to Change the World](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-segway-personal-transporter.html): Investors predicted a billion dollars in first-year sales. The Segway sold roughly 140,000 units across its entire twenty-year lifetime.
- [What Happened to Tumblr, the Platform Yahoo Bought for a Billion and Sold for Pennies](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-tumblr-yahoo-billion-dollar-mistake.html): Yahoo paid $1.1 billion for Tumblr in 2013. Six years later, Verizon sold it to Automattic for $3 million. Here's the full story of how a culture platform got killed by the companies that owned it.
- [What Happened to Flickr, the Photo Site Yahoo Left to Die](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-flickr-yahoo-photo-sharing.html): Flickr once hosted nearly 2 billion photos and defined photo-sharing for a generation. Then Yahoo acquired it, removed the features that made it special, and left it to rot while Instagram ate its lunch.
- [Is There a New Tony Hawk Game? The Series in 2026](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-tony-hawks-pro-skater.html): No new Tony Hawk game is announced for 2026. The last one was Pro Skater 3 + 4 in July 2025, and its studio cut up to 90 jobs in April 2026.
- [What Happened to the Sega Game Gear, the Handheld That Deserved Better](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-sega-game-gear-handheld.html): The Sega Game Gear had superior hardware, full color graphics, and backlit brilliance. So why did it lose to the Game Boy? Discover the tragic tale of ambitious hardware sabotaged by battery life and Sega's own chaos.
- [What Happened to SimCity and How EA Destroyed It](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-simcity-ea.html): From Will Wright’s revolutionary city builder to EA’s catastrophic always-online launch, the rise and fall of SimCity is a cautionary tale about corporate mismanagement.
- [What Happened to Commodore, the Company That Won and Lost](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-commodore-computers.html): Commodore sold more home computers than anyone in history. Then its own executives drove it into the ground. Here is how it all fell apart.
- [What Happened to Neopets, the Virtual World That Raised a Generation](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-neopets-virtual-world.html): From 150 million accounts and $160 million acquisitions to corporate neglect and a management buyout. The full story of how Neopets rose, fell, and tried to come back.
- [Why the Atari Jaguar Failed and What It Costs Now](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-atari-jaguar-64-bit-console.html): The Atari Jaguar sold about 125,000 units before Atari quit hardware in 1996. Sealed consoles have since gone for $1,199.99.
- [Is WordPerfect Still Around in 2026? Corel Sells It](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-wordperfect-word-processor.html): WordPerfect is still sold in 2026 by Corel, owned by Vector Capital since May 2026, but the last new version shipped in 2021.
- [What Happened to Lycos, the Search Engine Worth $12 Billion?](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-lycos-search-engine.html): Lycos went from Carnegie Mellon research project to the most visited site on the internet. Then it was sold for $36 million.
- [Is HD DVD Still Around? Why It Lost to Blu-ray](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-hd-dvd-format-war.html): HD DVD is dead: Toshiba quit on February 19, 2008, after Warner Bros. went Blu-ray exclusive. The retreat cost the company about $1.1 billion.
- [Is Lotus 1-2-3 Still Around? IBM Killed It in 2013](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-lotus-1-2-3-spreadsheet.html): Lotus 1-2-3 is discontinued: IBM stopped selling it on June 11, 2013 and ended support in 2014. It once held 70% of the spreadsheet market.
- [Do They Still Make Netbooks? Why the Eee PC Died](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-netbooks-laptops.html): No. Netbooks peaked at 38.8 million units in 2010 and died in 2012. Chromebooks under $200 and cheap Windows laptops replaced them.
- [Who Owns Gateway Computers Now? Acer Still Does](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-gateway-2000-cow-box-computer.html): Gateway computers still exist as a brand: Acer bought the company in 2007 for $710 million and now sells Gateway laptops only through Walmart.
- [Why Boo.com Failed and Who Owns the Domain Now](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-boo-com-fashion-dot-com.html): Boo.com burned $135 million in 18 months and collapsed on 18 May 2000. Hostelworld holds the domain now, bought out of a $375,000 fire sale.
- [Motorola Razr V3: 130 Million Sold, No Signal Left](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/motorola-razr-v3-coolest-phone-ever-made.html): The Motorola Razr V3 sold 130 million units, and since August 3, 2026 it cannot make a call in the US. What one costs second-hand now.
- [Is the Nokia N-Gage Still Around? Who Owns It Now](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-nokia-ngage-gaming-phone.html): The Nokia N-Gage is gone: Nokia stopped the hardware in November 2005 and closed the N-Gage service in 2010, after 3 million of a 6 million target.
- [Is Excite@Home Still Around? AT&T Took the Network](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-excite-at-home-broadband.html): Excite@Home is gone. It filed for Chapter 11 in September 2001 and AT&T took the network for $307 million, about one percent of its $35 billion peak.
- [Why the Sega Saturn Failed and What It Costs Now](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-sega-saturn-console.html): The Sega Saturn failed after a $399 surprise launch in May 1995 and sold 9.26 million units. A working console costs $180 to $280 in 2026.
- [Why the Apple Newton Failed and What It Costs Now](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-apple-newton.html): Apple sold about 50,000 Newton MessagePads in three months, then killed the line in 1998. Why it failed, and what a MessagePad sells for now.
- [Is the Original Xbox Still Supported in 2026?](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-original-xbox-microsoft-gaming.html): The original Xbox lost support in 2006 and Microsoft closed its Xbox Live service in 2010. Fans rebuilt the servers, and 39 games still run.
- [Is AOL Time Warner Still a Company? What Is Left](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/aol-time-warner-merger-worst-deal-in-history.html): AOL Time Warner stopped existing in 2009. AOL is being sold to Bending Spoons for $1.5 billion; Warner Bros. Discovery holds the rest.
- [Is Kozmo.com Still Around? The Brand's Fate in 2026](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-kozmo-com-delivery.html): Kozmo.com died in April 2001 after a $280 million loss. Los Angeles grocer Yummy Foods owns the name now, and the site has been dark since 2023.
- [Is Circuit City Still in Business? Zero Stores Left](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-circuit-city-electronics.html): Circuit City closed its last 567 stores on March 8, 2009. The name survives online under an owner who bought it in 2016. Zero stores left.
- [Did Amazon Almost Go Bankrupt in the Dot-Com Crash?](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/how-amazon-survived-dot-com-crash.html): Amazon never went bankrupt, but it came close: a Lehman analyst gave it four quarters of cash. A $672 million bond bought the time it needed.
- [Is Webvan Still Around? The $830 Million Collapse](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-webvan-grocery-delivery.html): Webvan shut down in July 2001 after burning about $830 million. Amazon owns the name now, and its founder is back with a robot warehouse.
- [Why the Nintendo GameCube Lost the Console War](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/why-nintendo-gamecube-lost-console-war.html): The Nintendo GameCube sold 21.74 million units to the PlayStation 2's 155 million and died in 2007. Its games returned on Switch 2 in June 2025.
- [Is eBay Still Around in 2026? 135 Million Buyers](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/ebay-broken-laser-pointer-to-global-marketplace.html): eBay is still around in 2026: a public Nasdaq company with 135 million buyers and $79.6 billion sold in 2025. It started with a broken laser pointer.
- [Is RadioShack Still in Business? 2026 Store Count](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-radioshack-electronics.html): Is RadioShack still in business? Yes, as a brand. The US chain died in the 2017 bankruptcy, and an El Salvador group has owned the name since 2023.
- [Is Friendster Still Around? It Came Back in 2026](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-friendster-social-network.html): Friendster deleted every profile in 2011 and shut down in 2015, but the name relaunched in April 2026 as an app with no ads and no algorithm.
- [Is Fry's Electronics Still Around? All 31 Stores Closed](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-frys-electronics.html): Fry's Electronics is gone. All 31 remaining stores closed on February 24, 2021, with no bankruptcy filing and no farewell sale. Here is what is left.
- [Does Ask Jeeves Still Exist? Ask.com Closed in 2026](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-ask-jeeves-search-engine.html): Ask Jeeves became Ask.com, lost the butler in 2006, quit building its own search engine in 2010, and closed for good on May 1, 2026.
- [Is BlackBerry Still in Business? Yes, but No Phones](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-blackberry-smartphone.html): BlackBerry still exists, but it has not made a phone since 2016. It earned $549.1 million in fiscal 2026 from car software and secure messaging.
- [Is Digg Still Around in 2026? Yes, as an AI Site](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-digg-social-news.html): Digg still exists in 2026, but as an AI news aggregator run by Kevin Rose, not a Reddit rival. The relaunched app shut down on March 14, 2026.
- [Is Encarta Still Available? Why Microsoft Killed It](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-microsoft-encarta.html): Microsoft Encarta is gone: disc sales ended in June 2009 and MSN Encarta closed October 31, 2009. What replaced it, and how to run it now.
- [How MySpace Lost to Facebook and Sold for $35M](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/rise-and-fall-of-myspace.html): MySpace lost to Facebook after News Corporation tied the site to a $900 million Google ad deal. It sold for $35 million in June 2011.
- [Is Google Glass Still Around? Discontinued in 2023](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/why-google-glass-actually-failed.html): Google Glass is discontinued: sales ended March 15, 2023 and support that September. What the $1,500 headset was, and what Google sells now.
- [Is the Microsoft Zune Still Around? Why It Failed](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/why-microsoft-zune-actually-failed.html): Microsoft Zune hardware died in 2011 and its services in 2015. Here is why it lost to the iPod, and what a used Zune HD costs in 2026.
- [Why Pets.com Failed and Where the Sock Puppet Went](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/why-pets-com-failed-dot-com-bubble.html): Pets.com sold pet food below cost, IPO'd at $11 in February 2000 and shut its store that November. PetSmart owns the domain; the sock puppet outlived it.
- [Why Google+ Failed and When Google Shut It Down](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/why-google-plus-actually-failed.html): Google+ shut down on April 2, 2019 and Google Currents followed in 2023. Here is why a $585 million social network sat empty.
- [Why Sega Stopped Making Consoles After Dreamcast](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/why-sega-stopped-making-consoles-dreamcast.html): Sega stopped making consoles on January 31, 2001, after the Dreamcast sold 9.13 million units. It has not built one since, and still will not.
- [Palm Pilot Explained: The PDA That Phones Replaced](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-palm-pilot-pda.html): The Palm Pilot sold a million units in 18 months, then lost to the smartphone. Palm shipped its last handhelds in October 2005.
- [Who Owns MapQuest Now? System1 and the 2026 Surge](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/how-mapquest-lost-to-google-maps.html): MapQuest is still around in 2026, owned by ad tech firm System1 since 2019. Google Maps only passed it in January 2009, by 700,000 users.
- [Was Apple Really 90 Days From Bankruptcy in 1997?](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/when-apple-almost-went-bankrupt-1997.html): Apple lost $1.04 billion in fiscal 1997 and Steve Jobs called it 90 days from insolvent. Microsoft's $150 million check landed on August 6, 1997.

- [Why the Nintendo GameCube Lost the Console War](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/why-nintendo-gamecube-lost-console-war.html): The Nintendo GameCube sold 21.74 million units to the PlayStation 2's 155 million and died in 2007. Its games returned on Switch 2 in June 2025.
- [Are Tamagotchis Still Made in 2026? Yes, by Bandai](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/tamagotchi-digital-pet-that-made-us-feel.html): Tamagotchi is still made by Bandai in 2026. Shipments passed 100 million in July 2025, new models cost $44.99, and 1997 originals fetch $40 to $50.
- [Why Sega Stopped Making Consoles After Dreamcast](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/why-sega-stopped-making-consoles-dreamcast.html): Sega stopped making consoles on January 31, 2001, after the Dreamcast sold 9.13 million units. It has not built one since, and still will not.
- [Microsoft Tried to Buy Nintendo and Got Laughed At](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/microsoft-tried-buy-nintendo.html): Microsoft tried to buy Nintendo in 1999 and spent an hour being laughed at. The letter survives, and the Xbox shipped two years later.

## Then vs Now
- [How Many Payphones Are Left? The FCC Stopped Counting](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/payphones-left-united-states.html): How many payphones are left? The FCC's last count found under 100,000 in 2016, then it quit counting in 2018. New York held one in five of them.
- [Are LaserDiscs Worth Anything? The 2026 Collector Market](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/laserdisc-value-collector-market.html): Most LaserDiscs are worth under $5, but scarce pressings run into the hundreds. Tokyo Raiders, the last title ever released, has fetched $5,700.
- [Are Heelys Still Sold in 2026? Who Owns Them Now](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/heelys-still-sold-2026.html): Heelys are still sold new in 2026, owned by BBC International, which paid $11 million for the brand in 2021. Peak year: 6.2 million pairs in 2006.
- [Why Discovery Zone Failed and What's Left in 2026](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/discovery-zone-failed-indoor-playground.html): Discovery Zone failed after two bankruptcies and closed for good by the end of 2001. One unaffiliated center still uses the name in 2026.
- [How Many Rainforest Cafes Are Left? 16 in the US](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/rainforest-cafe-locations-left.html): Rainforest Cafe is down to 16 US restaurants in 11 states in 2026, from a peak of 59. Landry's owns it, and the Paris location closes in November.
- [Who Owns Kinko's Now? FedEx Retired the Brand](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-kinkos-still-around.html): Kinko's is gone in the US: FedEx bought it for $2.4 billion, then took an $891 million charge in 2008 to stop using the name.
- [How Many KB Toys Stores Are Left? Zero Since 2009](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/kb-toys-stores-left.html): How many KB Toys stores are left? Zero. All 461 closed by February 9, 2009, and the brand now survives online and at a Comic-Con booth.
- [Where Is FAO Schwarz Now? Inside Rockefeller Center](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/fao-schwarz-store-rockefeller-center.html): FAO Schwarz is still open, but not on Fifth Avenue. The flagship moved to 30 Rockefeller Plaza in 2018, and Nordstrom shops followed in 2026.
- [Is Woolworth Still in Business? Only as Foot Locker](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-woolworth-still-in-business.html): Woolworth is still in business, but only as Foot Locker: it renamed itself in 2001, four years after shutting all 400 US five-and-dime stores.
- [Is the Disney Store Still Open? 21 Left in 2026](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-disney-store-still-open.html): The Disney Store is still open, but only about 21 locations are left in North America in 2026, down from 747 stores at the 1999 peak.
- [Can You Still Get Dial-Up Internet? NetZero Does](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/dial-up-internet-still-available-2026.html): Can you still get dial-up internet? Yes. NetZero, Juno and Microsoft's MSN all sell it in 2026, a year after AOL shut its dialer for good.
- [Scan Old Photos and Negatives: DIY vs Mail-In Cost](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/scan-old-photos-negatives-2026.html): Scan old photos at home or mail them out: a prepaid box of about 1,800 prints runs $145 in 2026, and 400 ppi is the resolution to use.
- [Who Owns Borders Now? The $13.9 Million Brand Sale](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/who-owns-borders-now-bookstore.html): Borders closed its last US stores in September 2011. Barnes & Noble owns the name now, bought for $13.9 million with 48 million customer records.
- [Is Hollywood Video Still Around? Every Store Closed](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-hollywood-video-still-around.html): Hollywood Video is gone. Movie Gallery liquidated the last 1,900-plus US stores in 2010, and its late fees chased 3.3 million customers for years.
- [Is Barnes and Noble Still Open? 720+ Stores in 2026](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-barnes-and-noble-still-open.html): Barnes and Noble is still open and growing: more than 720 US stores in 2026, with 60 more planned. Elliott has owned the chain since 2019.
- [Who Owns Claire's Now? The $140 Million Buyout](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/who-owns-claires-now.html): Claire's is owned by Ames Watson, which bought the chain out of bankruptcy in 2025 for about $140 million. Roughly 900 stores are still open.
- [How Many Boston Market Locations Are Left in 2026?](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/boston-market-locations-left.html): Boston Market is down to about six listed locations in 2026, and only three answered the phone. It had 1,143 restaurants in 1998. Here is what closed them.

It got crushed by a $90 gray brick called the Game Boy. Here is exactly why.

- [Why Netscape Navigator Lost to Internet Explorer](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/how-netscape-lost-the-browser-war.html): Netscape Navigator lost to Internet Explorer because Microsoft gave IE away free and wired it into Windows. Navigator led 51% to 40% in 1997, then fell.
- [Windows XP Bliss Wallpaper: Where the Hill Is Now](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/windows-xp-wallpaper-bliss-story.html): The Windows XP Bliss wallpaper hill is real, on private land off Fremont Drive in Sonoma County, and it turned green again on 18 February 2026.
- [Y2K Explained: What Really Broke on January 1, 2000](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/y2k-bug-what-actually-happened.html): The Y2K bug was real and the US spent about $100 billion killing it. Here is what still broke on January 1, 2000, from spy satellites to slot machines.
- [Did Napster Kill the Music Industry? The 2026 Math](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/napster-destroyed-music.html): Napster did not kill the music industry. US revenue fell from $14.6 billion in 1999 to $8.5 billion in 2009, then hit a record $11.5 billion in 2025.

## Money & Tech
- [Why Montgomery Ward Failed and Who Owns It Now](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/montgomery-ward-failed-who-owns-it.html): Montgomery Ward closed all 250 stores in 2001 after 128 years. Colony Brands has owned the name since 2008 and sells it online at wards.com.
- [Are LaserDiscs Worth Anything? The 2026 Collector Market](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/laserdisc-value-collector-market.html): Most LaserDiscs are worth under $5, but scarce pressings run into the hundreds. Tokyo Raiders, the last title ever released, has fetched $5,700.
- [Are Heelys Still Sold in 2026? Who Owns Them Now](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/heelys-still-sold-2026.html): Heelys are still sold new in 2026, owned by BBC International, which paid $11 million for the brand in 2021. Peak year: 6.2 million pairs in 2006.
- [Is Columbia House Still Around? The 2026 Shutdown](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-columbia-house-still-around.html): Columbia House stops taking new orders after September 15, 2026, closing after 71 years. The club peaked in 1996 with 16 million members.
- [Who Owns Yahoo Now? The $5 Billion Apollo Takeover](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/who-owns-yahoo-now.html): Yahoo is owned by Apollo Global Management, which paid about $5 billion in 2021. Verizon kept 10 percent. Microsoft once offered $44.6 billion.
- [Who Owns Sears Now, and How Many Stores Are Left?](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/who-owns-sears-now-stores-left.html): Sears is owned by Eddie Lampert's Transformco and it is still trading. The last count found five full-line stores left, down from about 3,500.
- [Why Iridium Failed: The $5 Billion Satellite Phone](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/iridium-satellite-phone-failure.html): Iridium put 66 satellites in orbit for about $5 billion, opened for business in 1998, and filed for bankruptcy nine months later. It sold for $25 million.
- [The Beanie Babies Bubble: How a $5 Toy Went Bust](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/beanie-babies-bubble-what-happened.html): Beanie Babies were a $5 toy people traded like stocks in 1998. How Ty Inc. built the bubble, why it burst in 1999, and what the bears are worth now.
- [theGlobe.com Today: The 606% IPO That Left a Shell](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-theglobe-com-dot-com-ipo.html): theGlobe.com is now an empty shell company with no employees and $15,115 in cash. Its 1998 IPO closed up 606 percent, a record that still stands.
- [What Happened to Wine.com and the Internet Wine Wars](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-wine-com-internet-wine-wars.html): Three companies burned through more than $200M trying to sell wine online between 1995 and 2001. The smallest one ended up owning the Wine.com domain.
- [What Happened to Lycos, the Search Engine Worth $12 Billion?](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-lycos-search-engine.html): Lycos went from Carnegie Mellon research project to the most visited site on the internet. Then it was sold for $36 million.
- [Is Craigslist Still Around in 2026? Who Owns It Now](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-craigslist-ugliest-website-worth-billions.html): Craigslist is still online in 2026 and still owned by Craig Newmark and Jim Buckmaster, but revenue fell from $1.034 billion to $302 million.
- [Why Boo.com Failed and Who Owns the Domain Now](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-boo-com-fashion-dot-com.html): Boo.com burned $135 million in 18 months and collapsed on 18 May 2000. Hostelworld holds the domain now, bought out of a $375,000 fire sale.
- [Is Excite@Home Still Around? AT&T Took the Network](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-excite-at-home-broadband.html): Excite@Home is gone. It filed for Chapter 11 in September 2001 and AT&T took the network for $307 million, about one percent of its $35 billion peak.
- [Is AOL Time Warner Still a Company? What Is Left](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/aol-time-warner-merger-worst-deal-in-history.html): AOL Time Warner stopped existing in 2009. AOL is being sold to Bending Spoons for $1.5 billion; Warner Bros. Discovery holds the rest.
- [Did Amazon Almost Go Bankrupt in the Dot-Com Crash?](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/how-amazon-survived-dot-com-crash.html): Amazon never went bankrupt, but it came close: a Lehman analyst gave it four quarters of cash. A $672 million bond bought the time it needed.
- [Is Webvan Still Around? The $830 Million Collapse](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-webvan-grocery-delivery.html): Webvan shut down in July 2001 after burning about $830 million. Amazon owns the name now, and its founder is back with a robot warehouse.
- [Is eBay Still Around in 2026? 135 Million Buyers](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/ebay-broken-laser-pointer-to-global-marketplace.html): eBay is still around in 2026: a public Nasdaq company with 135 million buyers and $79.6 billion sold in 2025. It started with a broken laser pointer.
- [Why Pets.com Failed and Where the Sock Puppet Went](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/why-pets-com-failed-dot-com-bubble.html): Pets.com sold pet food below cost, IPO'd at $11 in February 2000 and shut its store that November. PetSmart owns the domain; the sock puppet outlived it.
- [Y2K Explained: What Really Broke on January 1, 2000](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/y2k-bug-what-actually-happened.html): The Y2K bug was real and the US spent about $100 billion killing it. Here is what still broke on January 1, 2000, from spy satellites to slot machines.
- [What Is $1,000 From 1999 Worth in 2026 Dollars?](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/thousand-dollars-then-now.html): $1,000 from 1999 is worth about $2,000 in 2026. That is two weeks of a family health premium now, and it no longer buys the average PC.
- [90s Tech Prices in 2026 Dollars: Full 40-Item Table](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/90s-tech-inflation-calculator.html): A PlayStation cost $299 in 1995, or $655 in 2026 dollars. Forty sourced launch prices for 90s and early-2000s tech, adjusted with CPI-U.

## Music & Entertainment
- [Is Tower Records Still Around? Online and in Japan](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/tower-records-still-around.html): Tower Records is still around as an online store and a chain in Japan, but all 89 US stores closed after the 2006 bankruptcy auction.
- [Is Toonami Still On TV in 2026? Yes, on Adult Swim](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-toonami-still-on-tv.html): Toonami is still on TV in 2026: Adult Swim airs it Saturdays, midnight to 4 a.m. ET. Cartoon Network killed it in 2008 and a 2012 prank revived it.
- [Why G4 TV Failed Twice: The 1,000-Viewer Collapse](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/g4-tv-failed-twice.html): G4 TV failed twice. Comcast unplugged the gaming channel on December 31, 2014, revived it in November 2021, and shut it down again in October 2022.
- [How Many Sam Goody Stores Are Left? Exactly One](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/sam-goody-stores-left.html): Exactly one Sam Goody store is left in 2026, at a mall in Medford, Oregon. Musicland closed 226 of them in a single month in 2006.
- [When Did Netflix Stop Mailing DVDs? The Last Disc](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/netflix-dvd-mail-service-shutdown.html): Netflix stopped mailing DVDs on September 29, 2023, after 25 years and 5.2 billion discs. The last red envelope held a Blu-ray of True Grit.
- [Is Columbia House Still Around? The 2026 Shutdown](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-columbia-house-still-around.html): Columbia House stops taking new orders after September 15, 2026, closing after 71 years. The club peaked in 1996 with 16 million members.
- [Who Owns Napster in 2026? Every Owner Since 2001](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/who-owns-napster-now.html): Napster is owned by Napster Corporation, formerly Infinite Reality, which paid $207 million in 2025 and killed the music service on January 1, 2026.
- [Windows 95 Startup Sound: Brian Eno's 3.25 Seconds](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/windows-95-startup-sound-brian-eno.html): Brian Eno wrote the Windows 95 startup sound to a 3.25-second brief, made 84 versions, and did it on a Mac. The Library of Congress took it in 2025.
- [Is Blockbuster Still Open? The Last Store in 2026](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/is-blockbuster-still-open-last-store.html): Is Blockbuster still open? Yes, but only one store, in Bend, Oregon. Who owns the brand in 2026, how 9,000 stores became one, and what it sells.
- [What Happened to TechTV and The Screen Savers Channel](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-techtv-screen-savers-channel.html): ZDTV launched in 1998. Comcast killed it in less than a year after the 2004 G4 merger. Here is how a cable channel built for nerds disappeared, and where its hosts went.
- [What Happened to the Sony Discman, the CD Player That Changed Music](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-sony-discman-portable-cd-player.html): The Sony Discman made music portable on compact disc for the first time. Here is the full story of how it changed everything, then quietly disappeared.
- [Newgrounds Is Still Online in 2026, 31 Years Later](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-newgrounds.html): Newgrounds is still online in 2026, owned and run by founder Tom Fulp, funded by supporters from $36 a year, with its Flash archive kept alive by Ruffle.
- [What Happened to MiniDisc, Sony's Forgotten Music Format](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-minidisc-sony.html): Sony spent billions building the perfect portable music format. It conquered Japan, flopped everywhere else, and now Gen Z is collecting them on TikTok.
- [Was the iPod the First MP3 Player? Not Even Close](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/ipod-wasnt-first-mp3-player-heres-why-it-won.html): No: the iPod was not the first MP3 player. Korea's MPMan beat it by three years, in March 1998. Apple still won, and here is what did it.
- [Who Owns LimeWire Now? BabyDoge Bought It in 2026](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-limewire-file-sharing.html): LimeWire's file sharing died by court order in October 2010. The brand survived: BabyDoge bought it in September 2026, 8 million users and all.
- [Who Owns MTV Now, and Does It Still Play Music?](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/when-mtv-actually-played-music-rise-fall.html): MTV is still on the air in 2026 and owned by Paramount Skydance, but its last five music-only channels went dark on December 31, 2025.
- [Is Winamp Still Around in 2026? Yes, and It Works](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/what-happened-to-winamp-mp3-player.html): Winamp still exists in 2026: Winamp Group owns it, and the free 5.9.2 player runs on Windows 11. A Deezer-powered version lands in 2027.
- [Did Napster Kill the Music Industry? The 2026 Math](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/napster-destroyed-music.html): Napster did not kill the music industry. US revenue fell from $14.6 billion in 1999 to $8.5 billion in 2009, then hit a record $11.5 billion in 2025.
- [Did Blockbuster Turn Down Netflix for $50 Million?](https://404memoryfound.com/posts/blockbuster-netflix-acquisition.html): Blockbuster did turn down Netflix for $50 million in 2000. Netflix booked $45.2 billion in 2025 revenue; EchoStar now owns the Blockbuster name.
